text: iis, qui Colossis degunt, sanctis, fidentibus fratribus in Christo, gratiam et pacem a Deo Patre nostro, et Domino Jesu Christo.
note: *Patre* capital, God the Father (decision 20; *nostrō* lower case), as the same greeting in Rom 1:7, 1 Cor 1:3 and 2 Cor 1:2; *grātiam* lower case mid-sentence, as Rom 1:7 (*Omnibus, quī Rōmæ estis … grātiam et pācem*), where the address and greeting are one sentence; *iīs* lower case as the pipeline set it (1:1 ends with a comma) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Agimus Deo Patrique Domini nostri Jesu Christi gratias, semper pro vobis orantes,
note: *Patrīque* capital, God the Father (decision 20; τῷ Θεῷ καὶ πατρὶ τοῦ Κυρίου, NRSV "God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ"), as 2 Cor 1:3 *Deus et Pater Dominī nostrī* and 1 Cor 15:24 *Deō et Patrī* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Itaque nos, ex quo die id audivimus, non desinimus pro vobis orare, ac poscere, ut ejus voluntatis cognitione repleamini, cum omni sapientia, prudentiaque divina,
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 1:8 ends a sentence and *Itaque nōs* (Διὰ τοῦτο) turns from thanksgiving (1:3–8) to Paul's prayer for them (1:9–14), a new step, as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Agimusque Patri gratias, qui nos idoneos reddidit ad participandam sanctorum sortem in luce:
note: *Patrī* capital, God the Father (decision 20; τῷ πατρί, NRSV "giving thanks to the Father"), as 1:3 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Qui nos, ex tenebrarum potestate vindicatos, transtulit in regnum sui carissimi Filii,
note: *Fīliī* capital, the Son of God (decision 20; NRSV "the kingdom of his beloved Son"), as Rom 8:29 *imāginis Fīliī suī*; *Quī* keeps its capital after 1:12's colon, as the settled books do after a colon (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: in quo Filio liberationem habemus per ejus sanguinem, peccatorum veniam:
note: *Fīliō* capital, the Son of 1:13 (decision 20); *in* lower case as the pipeline set it (1:13 ends with a comma) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quoniam per eum visum est Patri, omnem universitatem inhabitare,
note: *Patrī* capital: Castellio supplies the subject of εὐδόκησε as the Father (KJV "it pleased the Father"; NRSV "all the fullness of God was pleased to dwell"), God the Father (decision 20) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Et vos aliquando mentibus alienos, atque hostes in prave factis,
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 1:20 ends the hymn of 1:15–20 with a full stop and *Et vōs aliquandō* applies it to the readers (1:21–23), a new step, as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Tum ut confirmentur eorum animi, caritate connexorum: tum ut tam divite, tam plena abundent peritia, ut Dei Patrisque et Christi mysterium percipiant,
note: *Patrisque* capital, God the Father (decision 20; TR τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, KJV "of God, and of the Father, and of Christ"), as 1:3 *Deō Patrīque* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quare nemo vos damnet ob cibum, aut potionem, aut festorum discrimen, aut novilunia, aut sabbata,
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 2:15 ends the account of what Christ did (2:9–15) with a full stop and *Quārē* (οὖν) draws the practical consequence, the warnings against food laws, feasts and angel worship (2:16–23), as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: “Ne tetigeris, neve gustaveris, neve attrectaveris”:
note: the precepts in direct speech, in the second person singular as the teachers give them (Μὴ ἅψῃ, μηδὲ γεύσῃ, μηδὲ θίγῃς; the BSB and NRSV quote them), not reported: not Scripture, so “…” without \\qt; the colon is Castellio's, outside, and 2:22 *Quōrum* answers them (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quamobrem necate vestra membra terrestria, impudicitiam, obscenitatem, libidinem, cupiditatem malam, et avaritiam, quae deastrorum cultus est,
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 3:4 ends a sentence and *Quamobrem necāte* (Νεκρώσατε οὖν) turns from the risen life (3:1–4) to what must be put to death; *cultus est,* with a comma, not the draft's full stop, as 1573's page (canvas 903: *quæ deastrorum cultus est, propter quæ inuadit*), the relative of 3:6 running on, as the Greek (ἥτις ἐστὶν εἰδωλολατρεία, δι᾿ ἃ) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: propter quae invadit ira Dei contumaces homines:
note: *propter* lower case: the sentence runs on from 3:5 (comma, as 1573's page *propter quæ*, canvas 903) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Induite igitur, ut Dei electi, sancti amatique, adfectum misericordiae, benignitatem, modestiam, mansuetudinem, patientiam,
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 3:11 ends a sentence and *Induite igitur* (Ἐνδύσασθε οὖν) turns from what is put off (3:5–11) to what is put on (3:12–17), as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ac quidquid vel verbis vel re facitis, id in Domini Jesu nomine facitote, Deo Patrique per eum gratias agentes.
note: *Patrīque* capital, God the Father (decision 20; τῷ Θεῷ καὶ πατρί, NRSV "to God the Father"), as 1:3; 1573 *Deo Patriq;* (canvas 903) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: De me omnia vobis exponet Tychicus, carus frater, fidelisque minister, et conservus in Domino.
note: paragraph, moved here from 4:8: the BSB's heading stands at 4:7 (Tychicus and the news, then the greetings), and the draft's \\p at 4:8 is one verse late, as its breaks in chapter 4 were laid by Castellio's numbering before 3:26 became the KJV's 4:1 (`Col.draft.edits.tsv`); 4:6 ends the exhortation with a full stop (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quem ideo ad vos misi, ut vestrarum rerum statum cognoscat, vestrosque confirmet animos,
note: no paragraph: *Quem ideō ad vōs mīsī* is the relative continuing 4:7's sentence about Tychicus (ὃν ἔπεμψα); the draft's \\p moved to 4:7 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: cum Onesimo, fido caroque fratre, qui vestras est. Ii vos de omnibus, quae hic gerantur, certiores facient.
note: *vestrās est.* with a full stop and *Iī* capital, not the draft's colon, as 1573's page (canvas 904: *qui vestras est. Ii vos de omnibus, quæ hìc gerantur*) and the Greek (ὅς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν. Πάντα ὑμῖν γνωριοῦσι); *cum* lower case as the pipeline set it (4:8 ends with a comma) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Salutat vos Aristarchus, meae captivitatis socius, et Marcus, Barnabae consobrinus, de quo mandata accepistis, si venerit ad vos, ut eum excipiatis.
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 4:9 ends the sending of Tychicus and Onesimus and the greetings of Paul's companions begin (4:10–14, *Salūtat vōs* … *Salūtat vōs* … *Salūtat vōs*), as Rom 16:21 opens its greetings from Paul's companions (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Salutate Laodicenses fratres, et Nympham, et ejus domus ecclesiam.
note: paragraph (the BSB's heading): 4:14 ends the greetings Paul passes on, and Paul's own greetings and instructions about Laodicea follow (4:15–17); the draft's \\p at 4:16 is one verse late, as at 4:7–8 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quumque lecta fuerit apud vos epistola, facite, ut etiam in Laodicensium ecclesia legatur, itemque ut Laodicensem epistolam vos quoque legatis:
note: no paragraph: the letter to be read at Laodicea continues 4:15's Laodicea (*Cumque*, καὶ ὅταν); the draft's \\p moved to 4:15. *Lāodicēnsem* capital, as 1573's page (canvas 904: *Lao-dicenſem* across the line; its OCR *Lao-*) and *Lāodicēnsium* in the same verse, for the draft's lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Salutatio mea manu Pauli. Mementote meorum vinculorum. Adsit vobis Dei gratia: Amen. \\cls Scripta est Romae, missa per Tychicum et Onesimum.
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m), Paul's own hand closing the letter, as 1 Cor 16:21 *Salūtātiō mea Paulī manū* opens its paragraph; the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it in italics under the verse (canvas 904) and as Rom 16:27, 1 Cor 16:24, 2 Cor 13:14; *grātia: Āmēn.* with the colon as 1573's page (*Dei gratia:Amen.*), where 2 Cor 13:14 has a full stop because 1573 has one there (Claude, 2026-11-11)
